title: Introduce KV memory sentinel and tiered spill orchestrator
author: Lena Park
description:
Motivation: production KV cache pressure causes repeated thrashing during mixed workloads (many small hot keys + large cold blobs). Existing evictors are reactive to occupancy but lack a lightweight, continuous signal to coordinate: (1) when to trigger asynchronous compaction, (2) when to allow spillback vs. immediate eviction, and (3) how to steer continuous batch scheduling to reduce tail latencies while preserving throughput. This PR introduces a lightweight 'memory sentinel' that maintains running histograms of segment utilization and page saturation, exposing a compact fragmentation gauge. The gauge drives a tiered spill orchestrator with three lanes: hot (no spill), warm (prefer soft eviction + migrate to compact segment), cold (spill to disk/backing store). The orchestrator implements spill gating to avoid cascading spill storms and integrates with the continuous batching scheduler so large batch windows briefly back off when spill I/O is active.

What changed (high level): added sentinel telemetry, a lane-aware orchestrator, soft-eviction path that prefers in-place compaction on idle, and scheduler backpressure hooks. This is intended to reduce eviction-induced latency spikes and reduce write amplification from repeated spill/reload cycles.

Design summary (single-string): The sentinel samples segment occupancy and per-segment free-run-lengths (to estimate fragmentation) and emits a single 8-bit fragmentation score per shard updated every 100ms. The orchestrator consumes per-shard scores and maps tenant/segment groups into one of three lanes using a cost model that accounts for recent miss rate, average resident size, and tenant priority. Soft-eviction attempts to coalesce small free ranges into compact segments if the node has been idle for >= 200ms; otherwise items are marked for spill. Spill gating uses a token-bucket per-node to limit concurrent spill jobs and a backoff multiplier when average I/O latency exceeds baseline.

Implementation notes: new files kv/cache/memory_sentinel.cc/.h, kv/evictor/tiered_orchestrator.cc/.h, kv/evictor/soft_eviction.cc, runtime/scheduler/spill_backpressure.h, tests/kv/sentinel_integration_test.cc. The sentinel avoids heavy locks by sampling with per-worker ring buffers and a merged view in the background flusher thread. The orchestrator exposes a small policy API so Dedicated and Private deployments can tune lanes via config. Interaction with continuous batching: scheduler now registers a callback that reduces max_batch_tokens by 30% while node-level spill tokens are depleted to keep tail latency bounded.

Benchmark summary: microbenchmarks on a 4xA100 node with mixed workload (90% small reads, 10% large cold writes) showed:
- 95p latency for small-reads dropped from 24ms -> 11ms under high memory pressure.
- Overall RPS stable; tokenized cost per request decreased ~6% due to fewer repeated spills.
- Spill I/O (GB/hour) decreased by ~21% in steady-state runs due to compact-on-idle.

Testing and rollout: unit tests added and expanded integration test harness to simulate mixed eviction patterns and scheduler interaction. Staged rollout: feature gated behind kv.memory_sentinel.enabled and orchestrator.mode=hybrid. Canary rollout plan described in PR body.

Compatibility and tuning: default policy is conservative (prefers soft-evict + compaction) and safe for on-prem installs; operators can adjust lane thresholds and per-node spill concurrency.

Related: references ENG-4722 (eviction reliability), ENG-5139 (scheduler batching SLO work), and a prior RFC RFC-evict-2025 (design notes).

release_notes: Introduce KV memory sentinel and tiered spill orchestrator: reduces eviction-induced tail latencies and spill I/O by coordinating soft-eviction, compaction-on-idle, and lane-based spill policies. Opt-in via kv.memory_sentinel.enabled.
